text.tspan: There is no terraform rollback: roll FORWARD to the last good code
Restoring an OLD state file (S3 version) ≠ rollback
it changes Terraform's memory, not AWS → next plan is wrong.
Only for a corrupted / deleted state.
Some changes can't be undone at all:
deleted RDS / S3 data, EKS version upgrade (no downgrade),
KMS key deletion → backups + guards BEFORE the change
Guards: small states (small blast radius), saved plan files, pinned module/provider versions + .terraform.lock.hcl,
lifecycle { prevent_destroy, create_before_destroy }, deletion_protection, final snapshots, S3 versioning,
dev → staging → prod promotion, blue/green (new node group / new ASG, then switch traffic)
Interview line: "I don't roll back the state, I roll forward the code: revert the commit, plan, apply. Data is protected
by snapshots and deletion protection, because Terraform can't bring deleted data back."
